**STEP 2 – Vessels:** The rice and vegetable plates look about 20 cm across (area ≈314 cm² each); the chicken plate about 18 cm (area ≈254 cm²).

**STEP 3 – Items:** Cooked rice, chicken mixed into/on the rice, a separate portion of chicken, mixed vegetables, and a dark drink. A little sauce appears to be on the rice.

**STEP 4 – Area:** On the rice plate, rice covers about 60% and chicken about 15% of the plate. Vegetables cover about 45% of their plate; the separate chicken about 50% of its plate.

**STEP 6 – Grams:** Using bulk densities of 0.8 g/ml for rice, 1.0 for chicken, and 0.6 for vegetables gives about 301 g rice, 94 g chicken on rice, 127 g vegetables, and 191 g separate chicken.

**STEP 7 – Energy:** Approximate cooked-food values are used; the small amount of sauce and dark drink contribute little.

**STEP 8 – Sanity check:** The portions look substantial and plausibly total around 700 g of food, plus the drink.
